investigation.title: Remote Agents: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocks All Agent Provisioning Evals
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-09-01T01:09–01:10Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm gateway ELB endpoint was unreachable during agent provisioning. Because the failure occurs at POST /api/agents before any agent identity is returned, zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were collected, causing a complete contract violation.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — the AWS ELB-backed service at the redacted us-east-2 endpoint that backs POST /api/agents → /v1/agents — was unreachable at the time of the eval run. Every remote-agents check depends on a successful POST /api/agents response to obtain an agent identity and VM assignment; because the gateway returned 502 immediately, the runner could not proceed past createAgent() and produced no evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure availability failure localized to the swarm gateway dependency of the production-api remote-agent provisioning path. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to production end-users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

investigation.summary: The eval-only check `published-observability-snapshot` failed because the published status.json at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json reported a snapshotAgeMinutes of 464, which exceeds the contract maximum of 300. All three sibling public-website checks passed, confirming this is an isolated eval failure scoped to snapshot freshness, not a broad public-website outage.
investigation.rootCause: The observability snapshot at the published URL was not regenerated within the required 300-minute window. At eval time (2026-09-01T01:10:28Z), the snapshot was 464 minutes old — approximately 2 hours and 44 minutes past the freshness deadline. The snapshot source field reports "desktop-nightly-release" rather than "github-actions", indicating the last successful publish came from a desktop nightly release process rather than the scheduled GitHub Actions workflow. The most likely operational cause is that the workflow or process responsible for regenerating and publishing status.json did not run or did not complete successfully within the expected cadence.
